question.knowledge_point: Determining Whether a Vector Lies on a Plane
question.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,-4,2⟩$, $c=⟨3,-10,2⟩$, and  $u=⟨-2,5,0⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
question.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -10 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s+3t=-2 \\ -4s-10t=5 \\ 2s+2t=0\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ -4 & -10 & 5 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & -4 & 4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=-2,$ which has no solution.

So, there are no values of $s$ and $t$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc=u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $u$ does *not* lie on the plane $Π.$
